title: The Downbeat Split
primary_metric: expected total studio minutes required to deliver a broadcast-ready take -- booked rehearsal minutes plus the probability-weighted cost, in re-booked session minutes, of a delivery rejected for missing the network's frame-accuracy tolerance

options.A: The Straight Cut — ship the already-rehearsed straight-subdivision arrangement and absorb the timing gap with a small tempo compromise
options.B: The Downbeat Split — rewrite the beat with a syncopated subdivision that hits the target duration exactly, at the cost of additional rehearsal time

sources.note: The CAA does not publish a distinct 'rehearsal-only' rate separate from session-call pay -- in-studio time (rehearsal and recording alike) is billed as one session call under this agreement. Overtime is billed at $44.34 per additional 20 minutes (one-third of the hourly fee). Re-verify before reuse past ~2027 in case a newer CAA scale has since been negotiated.

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4
protagonist: Elena Cross, staff arranger, Larkspur Sound
concept_sheet: The Downbeat Split — approved concept, provided directly by user 2026-08-24 (not from a CONCEPTS_*.md file)

deliverables.text: The Straight Cut's computed total running time: mixed-number beat length x mixed-number seconds-per-beat, multiplied across every phrase repeat, with full arithmetic shown.
A partial-phrase check: a fractional portion of the final phrase's mixed-number beat length, multiplied out to locate the target cutoff inside the running time.
The Downbeat Split's beat-subdivision calculation: the fractional timing gap divided by the ensemble's fractional subdivision unit, with full arithmetic shown.
A rehearsal read-through fit-check: mixed-number rehearsal time remaining divided by the length of one read-through of the syncopated passage.

A final decision table: rehearsal minutes required (mixed-number minutes-per-read-through x whole-number read-throughs), probability-weighted redelivery-risk minutes (a stated fraction x the mixed-number total booked session length), and expected total minutes, for both options, with a stated recommendation.

appendices.title: The Straight Cut: Phrase & Tempo Data
The Downbeat Split: Subdivision & Rehearsal Data

balance.argument_a: The Straight Cut books zero additional rehearsal minutes -- the ensemble already sight-reads it cleanly -- and absorbs the remaining timing gap with a small, uniform tempo nudge across the whole cue. Even after weighting in MA11's 1-in-3 redelivery-risk probability, its expected cost (30.0 min) is close to the Downbeat Split's -- and if MA11 is even slightly overstated, the Straight Cut wins outright.
balance.argument_b: The Downbeat Split is the only version that lands on the broadcast slot's target exactly, not approximately, and its rehearsal cost is small, bounded, and one-time: 9 read-throughs at the AFM's real published rehearsal rate. Because it is rehearsed to an exact target rather than delivered on a single live tempo adjustment, its redelivery-risk probability (MA12, 1/20) is far lower than the Straight Cut's (MA11, 1/3) -- and once that risk is priced in, its expected total cost (27.0 min) undercuts the Straight Cut's (30.0 min), reversing the raw-rehearsal-minutes comparison.
balance.margin_basis: Compute expected total studio minutes (rehearsal minutes plus probability-weighted redelivery-risk minutes) for both options (D5) and compare directly. Both options now carry a nonzero cost term, so the comparison is a genuine two-sided trade-off rather than a ratio with a structurally-zero numerator on one side.
balance.margin_note: RETUNED 2026-08-29 (case-write-stage remediation) -- the prior primary metric ('rehearsal minutes required per second of timing accuracy gained') was structurally unbalanceable: Option A's rehearsal-minute numerator was exactly zero by the case's own construction (already rehearsed; a continuous tempo nudge closes any residual gap exactly), so ANY nonzero Option B cost computed to a 100% margin under SPEC §2's formula, regardless of how the other ten assumptions were tuned -- confirmed the same structural pattern found in fret-board's QA precedent. Retuning a constraint could not fix this; the primary metric itself had to change. New metric: expected total studio minutes = booked rehearsal minutes + (redelivery-risk probability x total booked session length, MA2). This is grounded directly in FACILITATOR.md's pre-existing Twist (the producer's aside that a tempo-compromise take of this kind has already been rejected once, forcing a costly re-book) -- formalizing that narrative risk as MA11/MA12 rather than inventing an unrelated new cost. D1-D4 arithmetic is unchanged: D1 = 3 3/4 x 1 1/3 x 4 = 20 sec; D2 = 3/8 x 3 3/4 x 1 1/3 = 1 7/8 sec (1.875 sec); D3 = 3/8 / 1/2 = 3/4; D4 = 22 1/2 / 2 1/2 = 9 read-throughs. D5 rehearsal minutes unchanged: Option A = 0 min, Option B = 2 1/2 x 9 = 22.5 min. New D5 terms: Option A redelivery-risk minutes = MA11 (1/3) x MA2 (1 1/2 hr = 90 min) = 30 min; Option B redelivery-risk minutes = MA12 (1/20) x 90 min = 4.5 min. Expected total minutes: Option A = 0 + 30 = 30.0 min; Option B = 22.5 + 4.5 = 27.0 min. Option B is now the lower-expected-cost option. margin_pct = 100 x (loser - winner) / loser = 100 x (30.0 - 27.0) / 30.0 = 10.0%, well inside SPEC §2's ~20% cap and below the T1-09 15% 'wide' threshold. The original raw-rehearsal-minutes figures (0 min vs 22.5 min) are not deleted -- they remain the first two rows of D5's decision table, fully disclosed, so a student can see exactly how the risk-weighted terms flip the comparison. This margin is intentionally sensitive to MA11/MA12 (see sensitivity_note) -- that sensitivity is the case's real discussion content, not a defect to hide.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Real broadcast ad spots run in standard lengths (:15/:30/:60); this case's fictional client brief sets a specific frame-accurate figure inside that range, chosen so it lands exactly 3/8 of a phrase-repeat past the Straight Cut's written 4-repeat total (see MA4-MA7).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Sets the entire size of the timing gap the Downbeat Split must close. Changing it requires recomputing D2's cutoff location and D3's split to match, but the shape of the dilemma (A needs a compromise, B closes it exactly) is unaffected by moderate changes.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Total booked studio session length for this cue
modeling_assumptions.basis: A plausible single-cue booking block for a commercial session: one AFM minimum hour (Appendix C, S2) plus a half-hour of likely overtime, consistent with the ensemble already having spent part of the session rehearsing/recording the Straight Cut before Elena's decision point.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Governs how much time is left for new material (MA10), AND (since the 2026-08-29 retune) doubles as the re-book session length in D5's redelivery-risk term for both options. A shorter session value shrinks both options' risk terms, but shrinks Option A's proportionally faster (its risk term is its only cost), which can flip the recommendation toward A. Disclosed, not eliminated -- see case.json.sensitivity_disclosure[] and sensitivity_model.py.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Fixed directly by the case's own narrative ("the same sixteen-bar cue," Background).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Low -- scene-setting detail; does not enter the D1-D5 arithmetic, which runs on phrase length and repeat count rather than measure count.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Phrase length per repeat, straight subdivision
modeling_assumptions.basis: Author's choice of arrangement structure, sized so 3 3/4 beats x 1 1/3 sec/beat (MA5) is exactly 5 seconds per repeat with no rounding.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Jointly with MA5-MA6 fixes the Straight Cut's written total (20 sec) and, with MA7, the exact size of the timing gap.

modeling_assumptions.basis: A slow-to-moderate underscore tempo, chosen (with MA4) to multiply to a clean 5 seconds per phrase repeat.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Same as MA4 -- changing tempo changes the AFM-cost-per-second-of-accuracy ratio the whole case turns on.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Number of full phrase repeats across the cue
modeling_assumptions.basis: Author's choice of arrangement structure; 4 x 5 sec/repeat = 20 sec written total for the Straight Cut.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Sets the baseline duration the target (MA1) is measured against.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Fraction of the final phrase used in the partial-phrase check (D2)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Chosen so 3/8 x 3 3/4 beats x 1 1/3 sec/beat = 1 7/8 seconds -- exactly the gap between the Straight Cut's 20-second written total and the 21 7/8-second target (MA1), so D1 and D2 chain together with no fudge factor.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly sets the timing gap size; see MA1.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Eighth notes are the conventional "straight" default subdivision in staff notation (confirmed by search -- see RESEARCH_LOG.md); the case treats this as the ensemble's habitual sight-reading unit, consistent with Background's description of the Straight Cut as "clean straight subdivisions."
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: A coarser or finer subdivision unit changes D3's fraction-divided-by-fraction result but not which option is cheaper.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Rehearsal time per read-through of the new syncopated passage
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public data exists for how long one read-through of an unfamiliar one-beat syncopation in an otherwise-rehearsed 16-bar cue takes; the case fixes a value so the two options are comparable. Based on a full pass of the 16-bar cue at the case's slow 45 BPM tempo plus a reset/count-off.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly scales Option B's rehearsal-minute numerator in D5. Raising it much above ~4 minutes per read-through would make Option B's minutes-per-second-of-accuracy ratio grow and could make Option A more competitive.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Rehearsal time remaining in the booked session for new material
modeling_assumptions.basis: Total booked session (MA2, 90 min) minus time already spent this session rehearsing and taking the Straight Cut (Background: "the ensemble has already worked through the first one in this session"), chosen so 22 1/2 min / 2 1/2 min per read-through (MA9) divides evenly into exactly 9 complete read-throughs for D4.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: This is the ceiling on how many read-throughs Option B can afford. A smaller remaining-time value could push Option B's cost up or make it infeasible within the booked session, flipping the recommendation toward A.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Probability the Straight Cut's tempo-compromise take is rejected on delivery for missing the network's frame-accuracy tolerance
modeling_assumptions.basis: No published rejection-rate data exists for this specific failure mode (confirmed by search -- see RESEARCH_LOG.md); the case fixes a value in line with Larkspur Sound's own delivery history with this client, where a tempo-compromise take of this kind has already come back rejected once.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: This is the primary metric's single most load-bearing dial: a meaningfully lower value here can flip the recommendation from the Downbeat Split back to the Straight Cut. Disclosed, not eliminated -- see case.json.sensitivity_disclosure[] and sensitivity_model.py / tier2_probes.py --probe 5 --flex 0.5.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Probability the Downbeat Split's rehearsed, exact-fit take is rejected on delivery for the same reason
modeling_assumptions.basis: No published rejection-rate data exists for this failure mode either; set well below MA11 because the syncopated passage is rehearsed to an exact target (D3) across 9 full read-throughs (D4) before it is ever recorded, but deliberately not zero, since no live take is risk-free.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The answer is sensitive to this value -- see sensitivity_note and sensitivity_model.py.

sensitivity_note: MA1/MA4/MA5/MA6/MA7 jointly fix the size of the Downbeat Split's timing gap; MA2/MA9/MA10 jointly fix its rehearsal-minute cost; MA11/MA12 (redelivery-risk probabilities) and MA2 (re-book session length) jointly fix the risk-weighted term that now decides the primary metric. This 10.0% margin is genuinely close and is intentionally load-bearing on MA11/MA12 -- see sensitivity_model.py for the exact flip points.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: No published rejection-rate data exists for broadcast frame-accuracy QC (confirmed by search, RESEARCH_LOG.md P13); the true value is in principle measurable at a real studio but not publicly documented, so 1/3 is a good-faith estimate grounded in the case's own Twist narrative, not a discovered fact. sensitivity_model.py --flex confirms a -50% flex on this dial (1/3 -> 1/6) flips the recommended option from B to A; verify with tier2_probes.py --probe 5 --flex 0.5.

The re-book session length reuses MA2's stated 90-minute booking block rather than a separately-sourced 're-book' figure, since no published data exists for how long a redo session runs. sensitivity_model.py --flex confirms a -50% flex on this dial (90 -> 45 min) also flips the recommended option from B to A; verify with tier2_probes.py --probe 5 --flex 0.5.

derived.margin_pct_formula_note: margin_pct = 100 x (loser_total - winner_total) / loser_total = 100 x (30.0 - 27.0) / 30.0 = 10.0. Raw rehearsal-minute figures (0.0 vs 22.5) and the retired ratio metric are preserved above for continuity/audit; they are no longer the primary metric.

cohort_bands.note: The Socratic plan and Anchor timings in FACILITATOR.md run as written (0:00-45:00), with both deep-conflict threads at 20:00-30:00.

Anchors 2 and 3 combine into one pass (define the question and the process together). Run only one deep-conflict thread at 20:00-30:00 -- the 'is a zero-cost option really free' thread is the strongest single thread for a smaller room. The twist still drops at 15:00; total runtime shortens to roughly 30 minutes, not the content.

No vote to take at Anchor 1 -- the learner states an initial position instead. The guide plays devil's advocate directly rather than cold-calling. The twist still lands, but 'who reverses' becomes 'would you reverse your recommendation, and why' -- skip the deep-conflict threads and go straight from the twist recommit to Close.
